note.text: A diphthong is a vowel sound that moves between positions within a syllable. Phonetic symbols represent sounds rather than ordinary letter names. This lesson groups written model words; it does not play audio or test pronunciation. Accent conventions vary: the GOAT vowel may be transcribed differently in other standard models. Use the teacher's agreed model and a reliable recording to practise actual speech.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Model groups: boy → /ɔɪ/; choice → /ɔɪ/; go → /əʊ/; home → /əʊ/. A sound can have different spellings. A spelling can also have different sounds, so a letter rule cannot replace checking an unfamiliar word. Read the symbols as labels for the models, not as an instruction to pronounce two separate syllables.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Locate the relevant vowel in a model word, compare its transcription and group the written examples. Then practise the sound with a teacher or recording when available. Keep written recognition separate from an actual listening assessment.
